disclaimer: MODELED interpretation of an OBSERVED supply-chain map. Not a forecast and not investment advice. Areas worth investigating, not securities to buy.
current_reality: Advanced AI accelerators are being built as complete packages, not as standalone chips. Public materials show active product and capacity work across logic wafers, HBM, advanced packaging, interposers, substrates, testing and data-center infrastructure. The evidence does not prove that any one step is the bottleneck today.
why_it_matters: The finished accelerator cannot ship unless these steps line up. The compute die, memory stacks and package must be qualified together; then the server and facility must have enough cooling and electricity to use them. A constraint in one step can leave capacity in another step unused.
what_it_means: If demand grows, affected groups include memory and packaging manufacturers, equipment and substrate suppliers, server integrators, and data-center operators. More demand may increase the value of qualified capacity, but concentration alone does not show that a supplier is short of capacity or that a shortage is binding.
if_this_scales: Conditionally, higher accelerator demand could pull qualified HBM and package capacity together. If packaging expands faster than memory, attention may move to HBM or stacking; if packages ship faster than sites can energize, power and cooling could delay deployment. These are scenarios, not established outcomes.
what_could_happen_next: The next observable step could be a disclosed ramp in a specific accelerator package, followed by evidence about HBM qualification, package yield, substrate supply, test throughput or site energization. Which dependency matters most cannot be determined from this map alone.
concentration_migration: The first concentration signal is specialized advanced packaging and interposer attach. With relief, attention may migrate to HBM qualification, shared bonding tools, substrate yield or data-center power. This is a dependency sequence, not a calculated ranking.
gains_leverage: Qualified advanced-packaging capacity and interposer ecosystems if accelerator volume arrives
HBM suppliers that can qualify and ramp the required stack generations
Bonding, inspection and test-tool capacity shared across package flows
Sites with available power, cooling and grid interconnection
loses_leverage: Treating accelerator announcements as equivalent to shipped, installed compute
Assuming a named supplier is sole-source or currently capacity-bound without primary evidence
Ignoring HBM, substrate, test and facility dependencies after wafer fabrication
Reading concentration signals as securities recommendations
second_order_effect: A package ramp can move constraints across layers rather than remove them: more CoWoS starts pull interposers and substrates; more HBM stacks pull bonding and test; more installed servers pull power, cooling and networking.
opportunity: Investigate which package generations have confirmed allocation, whether HBM4 qualification broadens the supplier set, how substrate and test yields change effective capacity, and which AI-factory sites have energization dates. Do not infer a supplier investment thesis from this map.

confirm: TSMC or other primary sources continue describing advanced-packaging capacity as tight or expansion-constrained
HBM suppliers report demand exceeding available qualified supply
Package substrate or test providers disclose AI-related allocation or lead-time pressure
Data-center operators disclose power interconnection as a deployment gate
invalidate: Advanced-packaging suppliers report spare qualified capacity and normalized lead times
Multiple HBM suppliers report sustained unused qualified capacity
Large packages move to alternate flows without package-yield or substrate constraints
AI cluster deployments proceed without incremental power or cooling constraints

confidence.rationale: The existence of the process chain and named capabilities is supported by primary product and company materials. Concentration, migration and scale consequences are modeled inferences; no single current bottleneck is asserted.

next_question: When the next accelerator package is ready to ship, which dependency has a dated, qualified capacity signal: HBM4, advanced packaging, substrate, test, or site power?
